2019 
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4876 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioner/accused No.1 seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.148 of 2019 of Badvel Rural Police Station, YSR Kadapa District, which was registered against him and others for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of IPC and Sections 57, 58 R/w. Sections 26 and 30 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Badvel Rural Police Station, YSR Kadapa District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 05.08.2019 at 10.00 a.m., when the complainant along with her staff was moving in police jeep in Srinivasapuram village surroundings,
and on receiving credible information while she along with the panchayatdars went near Srinivasapuram check post, found the petitioner and on interrogation both of them confessed to have carrying the banned tobacco products in their white plastic bags and as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same,
registered F.I.R. for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.

He UDPR,J relied upon the order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch,
dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the Petitioner/A-1 for the offences under Sections 188, 272,
273 and 328 of IPC and Sections 57, 58 R/w.
Sections 26 and 30 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
5. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.

_ __ U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J Date:22.08.2019 Dsh Shaik Ibrahim vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 22 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40519824/
